title: Week 1 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “financial goal”?
options: A recurring cost that is relatively stable during the planning period.
Assets or rights received from a deceased person through beneficiary designation, will, trust, or law.
A notice asking creditors to take additional identity-verification steps.
A specific, measurable, time-bound outcome involving money or resources.
questions.explanation: Financial goal means a specific, measurable, time-bound outcome involving money or resources.
choices: A recurring cost that is relatively stable during the planning period.

A sacrifice of one benefit in order to obtain another.
A pooled investment vehicle issuing shares and holding a portfolio under a stated strategy.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “present bias”?
options: An eligible federal student loan on which government pays specified interest during qualifying periods.
Property value minus debt secured by the property.
A provision specifying duties, rights, price, duration, renewal, or remedy.
The tendency to overweight immediate rewards relative to future consequences.

A transaction account designed for payments, withdrawals, and deposits.
The tendency to experience losses as more significant than equivalent gains.

A tax based on assessed property value, commonly supporting local services.
A tax based on taxable income under applicable law.

The amount borrowed or remaining loan balance before interest and fees.
An amount that directly reduces tax liability when allowed.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates mastery of the Week 1 inquiry?
options: A student accepts the first available claim or offer without checking the source, terms, evidence, or consequences.
A student delays a high-pressure decision, compares total cost and alternatives, and documents the value and goal being served.
A student selects an answer only because it sounds confident, even when the record is incomplete or contradictory.
A student relies on political identity, advertising, or personal preference as a substitute for documented analysis.
questions.explanation: A student delays a high-pressure decision, compares total cost and alternatives, and documents the value and goal being served.
